messages.subject: Turn-trigrams
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I was wondering if anyone could help me with this question:

I am investigating turntaking patterns in conversational narrative, based on my Narrative Corpus (NC) ( cf. Rühlemann & O'Donnell forthcoming [in Stephan's journal CLLT]), a corpus of conversational narratives in which turns have been annotated in terms of the participant's role in the storytelling such as Primary Narrator, Responsive Recipient, etc. Specifically, I am interested in one particular turntaking pattern which Sacks (1992) has claimed is constitutive of three-party conversational narrative: the control of 'every third turn, from a first'; in terms of turn-trigrams: Narrator-Recipient-Narrator (N-R-N trigram). I have extracted a number of narratives with exactly three participants, one Narrator and two Recipients. I have also extracted for each story  the number of 'successes' of these N-R-N trigrams.

My question now is how these results can be examined in terms of significance. A test for binomial distribution does not seem to be appropriate since after each N-R-N success the next trigram is constrained in that it cannot but start with R-N, meaning that successive trigrams are not independent.

Does anyone have a better idea?

Thanks in advance

Chris

messages.subject: Control OpenOffice API from within R
messages.subject_clean: Control OpenOffice API from within R
messages.body_plain:
Hello corpus linguistics R-ists,

I recently saw a question posted on the Corpora-List asking about
batch converting Word .doc files to Unicode .txt files:

http://listserv.linguistlist.org/cgi-bin/wa?A2=ind1202&L=CORPORA&F=&S=&P=45290

One response suggested using Python to control OpenOffice.org's API
and convert any file OOo can open (.doc, .odt, etc.) to Unicode text
files:

http://listserv.linguistlist.org/cgi-bin/wa?A2=ind1202&L=CORPORA&F=&S=&P=46605

My question for you is:
Has anyone done this from within R? Possibly/probably using the
system() function, like was suggested for converting .pdf to .txt
here:

http://groups.google.com/group/corpling-with-r/browse_thread/thread/a9247be2d24b47b6

I don't know enough about OpenOffice's API, nor about APIs in general,
as the vast majority of my programming experience is in R, and
specifically in the R.app GUI on Mac.

I'd love to be able to run a loop over folders with .doc and/or .odt
files and convert them to .txt and then load them into R with scan().
I know that the text mining package "tm" has the readDOC() function,
which calls a local installation of Antiword to convert .doc files, as
discussed in this thread:

http://groups.google.com/group/corpling-with-r/browse_thread/thread/60c16e6c131848f9/e9fce67887095b3c

But I'd love to do this with OpenOffice (or LibreOffice) so as to open
either .doc or .odt, or anything else OOo opens.

Thanks for your time and expertise. Earl Brown

messages.body_plain:
Oh, a table, yes, that happens as the default as described in the
book. write.table converts a table into a data frame first and that
makes the first column be called Var1, for instance:

qwe <- table(sample(letters[1:5], 100, replace=TRUE))
write.table(qwe, file="x.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=FALSE)

Thus, if you make it a data frame yourself, you can tweak the names:

asd <-as.data.frame(qwe); names(asd)[1] <- "whateveryouwant"
write.table(asd, file="x.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=FALSE)

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
-----------------------------------------------
University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
